short-description: A built-in chaise alcove for reading, lounging and watching the woods from inside.
long-description: The Den's built-in alcove gives Walden an extra place to disappear between soaks. Stretch out with a book, watch the light change through the trees or stay exactly where you are until dinner becomes somebody else's problem.
name: Walden Den Alcove

short-description: A private Walden deck tucked into the trees on the creekside side of the property.
long-description: Step outside your Walden room and the forest gets immediately closer. The private deck gives you a quiet place for coffee, a nightcap or the long stretch between plans when the creek and trees are enough.
name: Walden Private Balcony

short-description: Big Catskills views with very little effort required on your part.
long-description: Windows, balconies and porches frame the mountains differently across the property. The common thread is simple: look up, slow down and let the valley, peaks and weather keep changing the picture.
name: Mountain Views

short-description: Shared living space for the crew when you take over Slide Mountain Haus.
long-description: When the whole Haus is yours, the living room becomes the place everyone eventually lands. Gather before the trail, recover after it or let the group scatter across the house and find its way back here.
name: Slide Mountain Haus Upstairs Living Room

short-description: A proper living room for game nights, slow mornings and your first-floor Slide Mountain home base.
long-description: The downstairs living room gives the two-bedroom Slide Mountain setup a shared center of gravity, with room to spread out before the trail, after Ralph's or during the highly underrated middle part of the day.
name: Slide Mountain Downstairs Living Room

long-description: A dedicated sitting area gives you a place for coffee, reading, conversation or staring out the window while pretending that counts as an activity. Around here, it does.
name: Sitting Area

short-description: A bedroom that does not have to do all the work.
long-description: A separate living room gives the stay another place to happen. Spread out, gather with your people or close the bedroom door and keep the conversation going somewhere else.
name: Separate Living Room

short-description: Your own wet bar for keeping the evening close to home.
long-description: A private wet bar gives the living space a little more independence. Pour a drink, make something cold and stay upstairs when the room is exactly where you want to be.
name: Lodge Private Wet Bar

short-name: Outdoor Patio or Balcony with Chairs

short-description: A proper kitchen and dining setup for doing the whole Upstate-house thing yourselves.
long-description: Opa's gives the group a full kitchen and dining area, so breakfast, dinner and the snacks between them can happen on your own clock. Cook together, assign one brave volunteer or ignore the kitchen entirely.
name: Opa's Full Kitchen

short-description: A vaulted living room gathered around a big river-stone hearth.
long-description: Opa's shared heart is downstairs: exposed wood beams overhead, the river-stone fireplace in front of you and enough room for the whole group to settle in without sitting on top of one another.
name: Opa's Cabin Living Room

short-description: A Marshall speaker for putting a soundtrack to the room.
long-description: Queue up the road-trip playlist, something slow for the bath or the record you forgot existed. The speaker is there when the room needs music and easy to ignore when the forest sounds better.
name: Marshall Speaker

short-description: A full kitchen with a casual perch for coffee, snacks and plans that may never happen.
long-description: Cook when you want to, then pull up to the breakfast bar for the informal part. It is useful space that makes a longer stay feel less like hotel living and more like having your own place Upstate.
name: Chalet Kitchen with Breakfast Bar

short-description: Room to spread out beneath the Chalet's wood-paneled cathedral ceilings.
long-description: Two lounging areas, big windows and a fireplace give the Chalet real living space beyond the bedroom. It is made for long mornings, late drinks and the kind of afternoon that accidentally becomes evening.
name: Chalet Living Room

short-description: A full kitchen for breakfast at noon, dinner at midnight or whatever happens in between.
long-description: The Chalet gives you a proper kitchen of your own, so the stay can feel more like borrowing a mountain house than checking into a hotel. Cook something ambitious, heat up something easy or leave it untouched and go to dinner.
name: Chalet Full Kitchen

short-description: A private place to stretch out somewhere that is not the bed.
long-description: The Cabin's sitting area gives the room a second rhythm: read by the fire, pour a drink, or do absolutely nothing from a proper seat before wandering back to the tub, porch or bed.
name: Cabin Sitting Area

short-description: A king bedroom tucked inside your own standalone Catskills hideaway.
long-description: The Cabin bedroom keeps the mood warm and private, with the bed at the center and the rest of the standalone space just beyond it. Close the door, settle in and let the woods handle the view.
name: Cabin Bedroom

short-description: One straightforward bed for a room that keeps things simple.
long-description: A clean, uncomplicated sleeping setup for guests who need one bed and would rather let the rest of the Catskills provide the decoration. Cowboy rooms are outfitted with Wright mattresses, designed around the things that actually make a bed good: balanced support, pressure relief, responsiveness and temperature control. What it means for your stay: A genuinely good bed waiting after the sauna, the trail, one more drink at Ralph's, or absolutely nothing at all.
name: Single Bed

short-description: One bed, one proper headboard outfitted with a Wright mattress and one very good excuse to sleep late.
long-description: A simple single-bed setup with a defined headboard and enough visual weight to make the bed feel like part of the room rather than something dropped into it. Cowboy rooms are outfitted with Wright mattresses, designed around the things that actually make a bed good: balanced support, pressure relief, responsiveness and temperature control. What it means for your stay: A genuinely good bed waiting after the sauna, the trail, one more drink at Ralph's, or absolutely nothing at all.
name: Single Bed with Headboard

short-description: A king bed anchored by the Penthouse's hand-crafted black-willow headboard.
long-description: At the top of the Lodge, the king bed gets a little theater from its hand-crafted black-willow headboard. It is part bed, part woodland sculpture, and exactly the sort of detail that makes the Penthouse feel unlike anywhere else in the building.
name: Lodge Penthouse King Bed

short-description: Two straightforward beds for a simple, flexible sleeping setup.
long-description: No extra ceremony here. Two separate beds give friends or family an easy place to sleep while leaving the rest of the room open for the parts of the trip that happen while everyone is awake.
name: Two Beds without Headboards

short-description: Two separate beds, each with a proper headboard and room to land.
long-description: A flexible setup for friends or family, with two distinct beds that make sharing the room easy without asking anyone to surrender their own corner of it.
name: Two Beds with Headboards

short-description: Thoughtful bath essentials for the soak, the shower and whatever comes after.
long-description: Everything you need to settle into the bathing ritual, from shower essentials to the small comforts waiting by the sink. Practical, considered and designed to keep the bathroom feeling like part of the stay, not a checklist.
name: Bathroom Amenities

short-description: A king bed with a little wilderness worked right into the pattern.
long-description: The bear-patterned Alpine bed brings a playful dose of mountain character to the room while keeping the important part simple: a generous place to sleep. Outfitted with Wright mattresses, designed around the things that actually make a bed good: balanced support, pressure relief, responsiveness and temperature control.
name: Alpine Bear Pattern Bed

short-description: A tucked-away nook made for reading, lounging and disappearing for a while.
long-description: A small room within the room. Settle into the alcove with a book, a drink or absolutely no plan, and let the rest of the suite carry on without you.
name: Built-In Alcove

marketing-subheadline: Penthouse view framed by the mountain light and sky.
short-description: A diamond-shaped window that turns morning light and mountain weather into part of the room.
long-description: One of Cowboy's unique architectural details: a diamond-shaped window framing treetops, sky and shifting Catskills light. It gives the room a view with a little more character than a standard rectangle.
name: Architectural Diamond Window

marketing-subheadline: Lodge Penthouse Living Room
short-description: A substantial private living room at the top of the Lodge, made for lingering between whatever comes next.
long-description: The Penthouse gives you more than a bedroom. Its private living room brings together vaulted windows, comfortable seating, a wet bar and room to settle in, with the social heart of Cowboy just downstairs.
name: Lodge Penthouse Living Room

marketing-subheadline: Cabin King Bed + Bunk
short-description: A king bed with an extra bunk nook, outfitted with Wright mattresses, built for a little more flexibility inside your private cabin
long-description: The Cabin keeps the sleeping setup relaxed: a proper king bed anchors the room, while the built-in bunk or lounging nook gives you another place to stretch outfitted with Wright mattresses, designed around the things that actually make a bed good: balanced support, pressure relief, responsiveness and temperature control.
name: Cabin Beds

marketing-subheadline: Alpine King Bed
short-description: A king bed dressed in the bold Southwestern pattern that gives Alpine its unmistakable Cowboy character.
long-description: The bed is the visual center of the room: a Wright king mattress layered with Pendleton warmth and a Southwestern-patterned headboard treatment that brings a little graphic swagger to Alpine without getting in the way of a very good night's sleep.
name: Alpine Bed Southwestern Print

short-description: Two proper beds for friends, family or anyone who sleeps better with a little territory of their own.
long-description: Two separate beds keep the room flexible for friends and families, with enough personal space to spread-out. Outfitted with Wright mattresses, designed around the things that actually make a bed good: balanced support, pressure relief, responsiveness and temperature control. What it means for your stay: A genuinely good bed waiting after the sauna, the trail, one more drink at Ralph's, or absolutely nothing at all.
name: Double Beds

short-description: Room to bring the little campers along.
long-description: These accommodations welcome families, with layouts that make it easier to stay together without giving up the breathing room that brought you to the mountains in the first place.
name: Family Friendly

short-description: Good things within arm's reach when leaving the room feels wildly unnecessary.
long-description: The in-room minibar keeps snacks and drinks close enough for a nightcap, a slow morning or the hour between a soak and dinner when getting dressed can wait.
name: Minibar

marketing-subheadline: Wifi Access
short-description: Wi-Fi when you need it. The forest when you do not.
long-description: Complimentary Wi-Fi keeps the practical stuff handled without asking you to stay glued to a screen. Check what you need, then close the laptop and get back to the mountains.
name: Wifi Access

short-description: A roomy walk-in rain shower for rinsing off the trail, the creek or a very long day of doing nothing.
long-description: Step into a proper walk-in shower with room to wake up slowly or warm back up after the woods. Simple, spacious and exactly where you want it after a hike, a soak or a cold morning.
name: Walk-in Rain Shower

marketing-subheadline: Paws welcome across most room categories.
short-description: Dog-friendly accommodations across most room types ($50/night pet fee) with access to 200 acres of outdoor trail space.
long-description: Don't leave your best friend behind. Most room types welcome dogs with open arms, custom water bowls, and acres of hiking trails.
key-benefit-or-selling-point-headline: What it means for your stay:
key-benefit-or-selling-point-description: Explore the wilderness alongside your dog.
name: Dogs Welcome

marketing-subheadline: Walden House and Alpine House reserved strictly for 21+.
short-description: The Walden House and Alpine House buildings are zoned exclusively for adult guests aged 21 and older.
long-description: To preserve a quiet, peaceful atmosphere for couples and solo travelers, our core soaking suites are strictly reserved for guests 21 and older.
key-benefit-or-selling-point-headline: What it means for your stay:
key-benefit-or-selling-point-description: A serene, uninterrupted retreat guaranteed.
name: Reserved for Guest 21+

marketing-subheadline: Easy access to Belleayre, Hunter, and Plattekill mountains.
short-description: Located just 15 minutes from Belleayre Mountain Ski Resort and short drives to Hunter Mountain.
long-description: Base yourself in luxury for winter sports. Enjoy quick drives to top downhill skiing, snowboarding, cross-country trails, and snow tubing peaks.
key-benefit-or-selling-point-headline: What it means for your stay:
key-benefit-or-selling-point-description: Spend less time driving and more time on the snow.
name: Proximity to Belleayre & Hunter Skiing

marketing-subheadline: Private trailhead connecting to Slide Mountain wilderness.
short-description: On-property trailhead located right at Slide Mountain Haus connecting directly to miles of Catskill wilderness trails.
long-description: No driving required—step right off the porch onto our network of private and public trails leading into the Big Indian Wilderness and Slide Mountain High Peak.
key-benefit-or-selling-point-headline: What it means for your stay:
key-benefit-or-selling-point-description: Instant outdoor adventure starting from your front door.
name: Direct Hiking Trailhead Access

marketing-headline: Gazer Fires & S'mores Under the Stars.
marketing-subheadline: Bluestone patio with communal fire pits.
short-description: Hand-laid bluestone patio with open fire pits, nightly fires, and complimentary s'mores kits.
long-description: Gather round the bluestone patio fire pits as evening sets in. Enjoy craft drinks, stargazing, and complimentary gourmet s'mores.
key-benefit-or-selling-point-headline: What it means for your stay:
key-benefit-or-selling-point-description: The communal heart of the lodge where stories are shared around the fire.
name: Dry Stone Patio & Nightly Firepits

marketing-subheadline: A 150-year-old tavern across the lane.
short-description: Historic tavern featuring craft cocktails, pub fare, and a restored 150-year-old two-lane manual bowling alley.
long-description: Step into Ralph's Bar for local beers, fireside tunes, and friendly competition on our vintage two-lane bowling alley across County Route 47.
key-benefit-or-selling-point-headline: What it means for your stay:
key-benefit-or-selling-point-description: The perfect casual evening hangout for drinks, music, and bowling.
name: Ralph's Bar & Vintage Bowling Alley

marketing-subheadline: Private access to Esopus Creek swimming spots.
short-description: Direct property access to pristine swimming holes and bluestone beaches along Esopus Creek.
long-description: Cool off in crystal-clear mountain water or stretch out on sun-warmed bluestone ledges along our private stretch of river.
key-benefit-or-selling-point-headline: What it means for your stay:
key-benefit-or-selling-point-description: Pure, unchlorinated summer refreshing right on the estate.
name: Creekside Swimming Hole & Bluestone Beach

marketing-subheadline: A hand-woven canopy net suspended 40 feet in the air.
short-description: Custom hand-woven Treenet installation suspended high in the forest canopy above the hiking trail.
long-description: Climb up into a massive, hand-woven hammock net suspended 40 feet above the forest floor for a unique bird's-eye view of the wilderness.
key-benefit-or-selling-point-headline: What it means for your stay:
key-benefit-or-selling-point-description: Unwind in mid-air surrounded by swaying trees and open sky.
name: 40-Foot Suspended Forest Treenet

marketing-subheadline: Authentic wood-fired sauna nestled in the woods.
short-description: A cedar wood-burning Estonian Iglu sauna surrounded by hemlock trees, complete with cold river plunge access.
long-description: Tucked into the forest along Esopus Creek, our wood-burning Estonian sauna offers deep thermal detoxification paired with refreshing cold mountain air.
key-benefit-or-selling-point-headline: What it means for your stay:
key-benefit-or-selling-point-description: Soothe tired muscles after hiking or skiing while breathing in fresh pine steam.
name: Estonian Wood-Burning Iglu Sauna

short-description: Private outdoor decks or covered porches attached to Walden, Alpine, Cabin, Chalet, and Lodge suites.
long-description: Equipped with rocking chairs, loungers, or soaking tubs, your private deck offers seamless indoor-outdoor wilderness living.
key-benefit-or-selling-point-headline: What it means for your stay:
key-benefit-or-selling-point-description: Morning coffee with the birds and evening nightcaps under the stars.

long-description: Enjoy the flexibility of preparing your own meals or hiring a private chef with complete kitchens and spacious dining areas.
key-benefit-or-selling-point-headline: What it means for your stay:
key-benefit-or-selling-point-description: Dine in with family and friends without ever leaving your private mountain chalet.

long-description: Built from native Catskill river stone, these massive fireplaces anchor the vaulted living rooms of our standalone chalets.
key-benefit-or-selling-point-headline: What it means for your stay:
key-benefit-or-selling-point-description: The ultimate centerpiece for family gatherings, wine tastings, or late-night stories.

marketing-subheadline: Fireside comfort at the flick of a switch.
